newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN DEBT MARKET STUCK WITH HEAVY TONE.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN DEBT MARKET STUCK WITH HEAVY TONE.

text.p: *Australian debt struggled for most of day as several factors combined to dampen the market's early rally. Yields finish with only modest movements on the day.
*RBA governor Macfarlane due to speak in Perth at 1300 GMT.
Australian debt struggled for most of day as several factors combined to dampen the market's early rally and yields finished with only modest movements.

Continued concerns about the performance of U.S. Treasuries after their recent steep sell-off, worries over a speech by Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane and the threat of the Bundesbank tightening its repo rate all meant that the local market was stuck with a heavy tone, traders said.
Macfarlane is due to deliver in Perth his first speech since last month's official rate cut to 5.0 percent and the central bank's partial gold reserve sales at 1300 GMT.

Trading was fairly choppy with the 10-year bond futures contract sprinting to 93.280 just after the opening, but from then on the market was backtracking and slithered to 93.180 at one stage before ending at 93.205.

"It's too early to say that we have seen a top to these markets," said Chris Bell, Director of Treasury at Dresdner Australia. "If the price went down another 10 or 15 points one would be a bit more confident to say prices had topped, and that we were in a new trend and the bull trend was broken."
The 10-year bond contract struck an all time high of 93.695 on August 1 after steadily rallying from 91.700 in early April.
Adding to the market's negative sentiment was a report by HSBC Markets saying that enterprise bargaining agreements have shown no sign of the wages slowdown in the second quarter.
HSBC forecast that agreements formalised in the June quarter would be around 4.7 percent, level with the March quarter.
"There is little evidence that earnings outcomes are responding to lower inflation," said John Edwards, chief economist at HSBC Markets.
"Earnings are persistently growing at more than twice the level of inflation," he said, adding this meant that unless output took off the gap would remain above productivity growth.

Yield spreads to the dollar bloc ended fairly mixed with the long-end giving up almost all of its initial tightening as the rally came off the boil. The local yield curve flattened slightly, reversing some of Monday's sharp steepening.
